c.tagline: The gateway to the rock-cut wonders of Ellora and Ajanta.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws are the main way around and rarely use the meter — agree a price first, or use Uber or Ola for a fixed fare.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified emergency number; 100 reaches the police and 108 the ambulance service directly.

avoid.reason: Touts around Ajanta/Ellora; caution at night

hood_desc: The walled old city around City Chowk, home to Bibi ka Maqbara (the 'mini Taj'), the historic gates and Panchakki water mill; the sightseeing heart, dense and atmospheric.
A planned, modern part of town with wide roads, malls, mid-range hotels and restaurants; a convenient, orderly base close to the airport and business district.
A busy central market and dining area lined with shops, street food and eateries; lively in the evenings and handy for shopping and a bite.

The old cantonment quarter around the railway station and Padampura, with tree-lined lanes, army bungalows and a cluster of station hotels; quiet, central and the easiest base if you are arriving by train.
lodging: Welcomhotel by ITC Hotels, Rama International, Aurangabad
Amarpreet, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar - Am Hotel Kollection

water.note: Drink only bottled or filtered water; tap water is not safe for visitors.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; auto-rickshaws operate all day and are the easiest option to find.
transit.note: There is no metro or suburban rail; the Aurangabad Smart City Bus network covers the main corridors, but auto-rickshaws are the everyday way to get around. Uber and Ola operate with a limited number of cars.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash on board (typically ₹10-30 by distance); auto-rickshaw fares are usually negotiated since meters are seldom used.

bus: MSRTC state buses to Mumbai, Pune, Nashik and the Ajanta/Ellora caves
train: Indian Railways: Aurangabad Junction, with trains to Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur and Hyderabad

transit.m: City bus or shared auto from Chikalthana to the center (~30 min)
Prepaid taxi or auto-rickshaw to the center (20-30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% at nicer restaurants is appreciated. A service charge is sometimes already added.

food.name: Naan qalia
food.desc: The city's own dish: mutton simmered with a dozen ground spices into a thin, fiery qalia, mopped up with tandoori naan. Said to date from Mughal army kitchens.

places.name: Great Sagar Restaurant
places.note: Widely named the benchmark for mutton naan khaliya, with rich gravy and fresh naan.

places.name: Naan qalia shops, City Chowk
places.note: Old-city counters cook qalia in big pots from late afternoon; cheapest and most traditional.

places.name: Yalla Yalla
places.note: Popular non-veg kitchen doing Mughlai mutton dishes alongside its biryani.

food.name: Aurangabadi mutton biryani
food.desc: Deccan-style biryani with long-grain rice layered over marinated mutton, mint and fried onion, milder and more fragrant than the Hyderabadi version.

places.name: Great Sagar Restaurant
places.note: Mutton biryani rated as good as its naan qalia by regulars.

places.name: Yalla Yalla
places.note: Richly spiced biryanis including mutton dum, plus shami kebab and achari chicken.

places.name: Gulmandi bazaar eateries
places.note: Old-city biryani houses serve by the plate from the handi until it is finished.

food.name: Tahri
food.desc: One-pot rice cooked with mutton or vegetables, potatoes and whole spice, less layered than biryani and the everyday festival rice of Aurangabad households.

places.name: Naan qalia shops, City Chowk
places.note: Old-city kitchens cook tahri alongside qalia, especially during Ramzan.

places.name: Great Sagar Restaurant
places.note: Serves the local rice dishes in their traditional Aurangabadi form.

places.name: Shahganj market food stalls
places.note: Market stalls near the mosque dish up rice-and-mutton plates at lunchtime.

food.name: Seekh kebab and tandoori mutton
food.desc: Minced mutton kebabs and chargrilled chops from the old-city grills, served with raw onion, lime and roomali roti after sundown.

places.name: Gulmandi bazaar eateries
places.note: Charcoal grills fire up in the evening, busiest during Ramzan nights.

places.name: Tandoor Restaurant
places.note: Long-running kebab and tandoori address favoured by visitors staying near the station.

places.name: Yalla Yalla
places.note: Shami kebab, prawn koliwada and grills alongside the North Indian menu.

food.name: Marathwada veg thali
food.desc: Jowar bhakri with pitla, spicy thecha, sprouted usal and bharli vangi - the region's dry-country vegetarian spread, served unlimited.

places.name: Bhoj Thali
places.note: Well-known unlimited Maharashtrian and Rajasthani thali; the easy veg option in town.

places.name: Latitude, Gateway Hotel
places.note: Hotel all-day dining that puts regional Marathwada specialities on the dinner menu.

places.name: Shahganj market food stalls
places.note: Basic bhakri-and-pitla plates cooked fresh for market traders.

food.name: Khubani ka meetha
food.desc: Dried apricots stewed with sugar until jammy, topped with cream or almond slivers. The Deccan wedding dessert and the sweet finish to a naan qalia meal.

places.name: Great Sagar Restaurant
places.note: Keeps the classic Deccan dessert on the menu after the mutton dishes.

places.name: Gulmandi bazaar sweet shops
places.note: Old-city mithai counters sell khubani ka meetha by weight, best during Ramzan and weddings.

places.name: Latitude, Gateway Hotel
places.note: Refined hotel version of the apricot dessert with cream.

food.name: Shahi chai and Irani tea
food.desc: Strong milky tea boiled with cardamom, sometimes enriched with khoya into a shahi cup. Non-alcoholic and served all day in the old city.

places.name: Gulmandi bazaar tea shops
places.note: Irani-style cafes pour chai with osmania biscuits from dawn.

places.name: City Chowk tea stalls
places.note: Small counters beside the qalia shops keep the kettles going late.

places.name: Tandoor Restaurant
places.note: Handy sit-down chai after kebabs for visitors near the station.

food.name: Laban, lassi and sugarcane juice
food.desc: Salted buttermilk laban, sweet thick lassi and fresh-pressed sugarcane juice with lime and ginger - the local coolers in a strictly dry old city.

places.name: Shahganj market juice stalls
places.note: Sugarcane presses and buttermilk sellers cluster around the market.

places.name: Gulmandi bazaar
places.note: Laban and lassi counters beside the mutton shops, drunk to cut the spice.

places.name: Bhoj Thali
places.note: Serves fresh chaas and lassi with its unlimited thali.

landmarks: Ellora Caves
A UNESCO marvel of 34 rock-cut temples where the monolithic Kailasa Temple, carved from a single cliff, ranks among humanity's greatest achievements.
Ajanta Caves
Buddhist cave sanctuaries hollowed into a horseshoe gorge, sheltering 2,000-year-old murals considered the finest surviving paintings of ancient India.
Bibi Ka Maqbara
Nicknamed the 'Taj of the Deccan,' this marble-and-stucco mausoleum built for Aurangzeb's wife mirrors the Taj Mahal's silhouette at a fraction of its fame.
Daulatabad Fort
A formidable 12th-century hilltop citadel with moats, dark passages, and the towering Chand Minar, once briefly capital of the Delhi Sultanate.
Aurangabad Caves
Twelve serene Buddhist caves carved into the hills just outside the city, adorned with intricate sculptures of bodhisattvas and dancing figures.
Grishneshwar Temple
One of India's twelve sacred Jyotirlinga shrines to Shiva, its red-stone spire and carved tiers draw pilgrims to the village beside Ellora.
Panchakki (Water Mill)
An ingenious 17th-century watermill fed by underground channels, grinding grain for pilgrims beside a Sufi saint's shrine and fish-filled tank.
Khuldabad (Tomb of Aurangzeb)
The austere open-air grave of mighty emperor Aurangzeb lies in this Sufi 'Valley of Saints,' a humbling contrast to Mughal opulence.
Salim Ali Lake
A tranquil urban lake and bird sanctuary named for India's famed ornithologist, framed by the medieval Delhi Gate of the old city walls.
Himayat Bagh
A sprawling 17th-century Mughal garden of mango orchards and old water channels, offering shady respite from Aurangabad's bustle.

train.note: No international trains. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) station has overnight services to Mumbai (about 7 hours) and trains to Pune, Nanded and Hyderabad, though the network here is thinner than in coastal Maharashtra. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead. Most visitors are here for Ajanta and Ellora, which are reached by road, not rail.

bus.note: No international coaches. MSRTC (https://msrtc.maharashtra.gov.in/) runs from the central bus stand to Mumbai (about 8 hours), Pune (4-5) and Nashik, and the state buses to the Ellora and Ajanta caves are the standard way to reach them. Private sleepers are bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/).

ferry.note: Aurangabad is inland on the Deccan plateau with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Paithan
half.blurb: Historic town on the Godavari River known for handwoven Paithani silk sarees and the Jayakwadi Dam gardens.

full.name: Lonar Crater Lake
full.blurb: Saline lake formed by a meteor impact tens of thousands of years ago, one of the few such craters in basalt rock.
